issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or losing forward gears
issues.sym: Slipping, banging or badly timed shifts, fluid leaks, or the car revving but not moving in Drive.
issues.why: The CD4E automatic has several Ford bulletins for lost forward engagement, including a snap ring that can shift out of place. Owners report failures around 50,000-75,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or will not move, stop driving it and get a transmission diagnosis; a rebuild or used unit is the usual fix.

issues.t: Clogged fuel pump filter can cause stalling (recall)
issues.sym: Hesitation, surging or loss of power when accelerating, getting worse over time until the engine may stall.
issues.why: The filter on the in-tank fuel delivery module can clog with contamination and starve the engine of fuel. Ford recalled these cars and extended coverage on the module.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. If the car surges or loses power, avoid busy roads until it is checked. Ask a dealer whether the fuel delivery module recall was done.

issues.t: Battery cable can short and cause a fire (recall)
issues.sym: A no-start, sudden stalling, or a burning smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: The battery cable can be routed where it rubs and shorts, which can cause a fire, a stall or a no-start.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Have a dealer check the battery cable recall.

issues.t: Brake lights can fail or stay on (recall)
issues.sym: The brake lights do not come on when you brake, or they stay lit all the time. The shifter may also stick in Park.
issues.why: The brake lamp switch can fail. Owners of later Cougars also report repeated brake light switch problems.
issues.next: Ask someone to check your brake lights. Have a dealer check the switch recall on 1999 cars.

issues.t: Rear brakes can lock up from a faulty valve (recall)
issues.sym: The rear wheels lock or skid during firm braking, and the car may feel unstable.
issues.why: The rear brake pressure control valves can malfunction. If both fail, the rear wheels can lock.
issues.next: Leave extra stopping room and have a dealer check whether the valve recall was done.

issues.t: Blower motor resistor can overheat and melt (recall)
issues.sym: The fan only works on some speeds, or a burning plastic smell comes from under the dash.
issues.why: An open circuit in the blower resistor can cause arcing that melts its connector, creating a fire risk.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Turn the fan off if you smell burning plastic. Ask a dealer about the blower resistor recall.

issues.t: Door may not latch and could open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: A door that seems closed but is not fully latched, or a door ajar warning that stays on.
issues.why: A door latch problem can keep the door from latching when it is shut.
issues.next: Check each door is fully closed before driving. Have a dealer check the door latch recall.

issues.t: Accelerator cable can stick (recall)
issues.sym: The gas pedal sticks or is slow to return, or the engine stays at high revs.
issues.why: The throttle cable can bind and hold the throttle open.
issues.next: If the engine keeps revving, shift to Neutral, brake firmly and pull over. Have the recall checked.

issues.t: Alternator failure, dim lights and stalling
issues.sym: The battery light comes on, gauges swing, dash lights brighten and dim, the battery goes flat, or the engine stalls while driving.
issues.why: The alternator wears out, and the connector on its wiring harness can be damaged and lose contact. Some owners replaced several batteries and alternators before the wiring was checked.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the charging system and the alternator connector checked together before replacing parts. Pull over safely if the gauges start acting up.

issues.t: Battery light on but charging seems fine
issues.sym: The battery warning light comes on, sometimes on and off, even though the battery stays charged.
issues.why: Ford found a blown or intermittent fuse could trigger the light on early cars, and on later cars the light could come on with a working charging system.
issues.next: Have the fuses and charging voltage checked. If charging tests fine, ask the shop about the Ford bulletins.

issues.t: Power steering fluid leaks and heavy steering
issues.sym: Power steering fluid drips under the front, a whining pump, or steering that feels heavier than normal.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for leaks at the high-pressure line where it meets the steering gear, and for high steering effort with leaks. Some owners needed a new steering rack.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Check the power steering fluid level and look for leaks. Running the pump low on fluid can ruin it, so get the leak fixed.
issues.sevReason: Fluid leak; heaviness builds gradually. First step covers sudden heaviness.

issues.t: Timing belt shredding (2.0L)
issues.sym: A slapping or scraping noise from the timing cover, or the engine suddenly quits.
issues.why: Ford found the 2.0L timing belt could shred or strike its front cover. A broken belt stops the engine.
issues.next: Have the belt inspected if you hear noise from the cover, and replace it on schedule if there is no record.

issues.t: Hard starting in freezing weather (2.0L)
issues.sym: Below freezing, long cranking or no start, sometimes with a fuel smell.
issues.why: The 2.0L can overfuel on cold starts and flood itself.
issues.next: Ask a shop about the cold-start bulletin and any engine computer update.

issues.t: Hard start or rough idle after a hot soak (V6)
issues.sym: After the hot engine sits for a short time, it is hard to restart, idles roughly, or hesitates.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for hot-restart and rough-idle problems on the 2.5L V6.
issues.next: Note when it happens and ask the shop to check the Ford bulletins for the 2.5L.

issues.t: Rough idle and stalling from cam timing codes (2.0L)
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes P1380, P1381 or P1383, a rough idle, stalling, or less power.
issues.why: The 2.0L has variable cam timing. Ford issued bulletins for these codes, which point to the cam timing control.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the variable cam timing solenoid and wiring checked. Keep the oil full and fresh, since the system runs on engine oil.

issues.t: Lean codes from vacuum leaks
issues.sym: Check engine light with lean codes (P0171 or P0174), a rough idle, or hesitation.
issues.why: Air leaks into the intake through cracked hoses or gaskets and upsets the fuel mixture.
issues.next: Ask for a smoke test to find the leak before replacing sensors.

issues.t: Check engine light for EGR flow codes
issues.sym: Check engine light with EGR codes such as P0401 or P1401, sometimes with rough running or worse fuel economy.
issues.why: The EGR pressure sensor or clogged EGR passages cause these codes. Ford extended warranty coverage on the EGR pressure sensor for many 2000-2003 vehicles.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the EGR pressure sensor and hoses checked.

issues.t: Hesitation or surge between 3,000 and 4,000 rpm
issues.sym: A stumble or surge when accelerating steadily through the middle of the rev range.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for this drivability complaint on 2002 cars.
issues.next: Ask the shop to check the Ford bulletins and any engine computer update.

issues.t: Cracked intake valves can damage the V6
issues.sym: A misfire, rough running, or a check engine light that can lead to serious engine damage.
issues.why: Ford found a batch of intake valves with tiny cracks that could damage Duratec V6 engines.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Have a compression test and ask a dealer whether your engine falls under the bulletin.

issues.t: Heater core leak
issues.sym: A sweet smell inside, fog on the windshield, damp carpet, or coolant loss.
issues.why: The heater core can leak. Ford issued a bulletin for heater core leaks on these years.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested and fix it before low coolant causes overheating.

issues.t: Shifter stuck in Park with the brake pressed
issues.sym: The shifter will not come out of Park even with the brake pressed.
issues.why: Ford found brake light circuit issues could disable the brake-shift interlock.
issues.next: Check whether your brake lights work and have the switch and interlock tested.

issues.t: Exhaust flange studs break and rattle
issues.sym: A rattle, scraping or louder exhaust noise from under the car.
issues.why: The studs at an exhaust flange can break, which lets the joint leak and rattle.
issues.next: Have the exhaust joint repaired. Exhaust leaks under the car can let fumes into the cabin.

issues.t: Rotten egg smell from the exhaust
issues.sym: A sulfur or rotten egg smell, mainly after hard driving.
issues.why: Ford found this odor on 2.5L and automatic cars, linked to how the catalytic converter handles sulfur in fuel.
issues.next: Try a different fuel brand. If the smell is strong or the check engine light is on, have the converter and engine checked.

issues.t: Fuel gauge drops to empty with fuel in the tank
issues.sym: The fuel gauge suddenly falls to empty and then recovers.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for the fuel gauge reading empty with fuel in the tank, tied to the fuel level sender.
issues.next: Track your mileage between fill-ups until it is fixed, and have the sender checked.

issues.t: Slow fill and pump nozzle keeps shutting off
issues.sym: The gas pump nozzle clicks off over and over and the tank fills slowly.
issues.why: A flapper valve in the filler pipe can stick. Ford extended coverage on this part.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the filler pipe coverage still applies.

issues.t: Low coolant light on with a full tank (V6)
issues.sym: The low coolant warning comes on even though the coolant level looks right.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for false low coolant warnings, including on the 2.5L.
issues.next: Confirm the level with the engine cold. If it is full, ask a shop about the bulletin.

issues.t: Power door locks lock and unlock by themselves
issues.sym: The doors cycle locked and unlocked without anyone pressing a button.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for door locks cycling without command.
issues.next: Have the lock switches and module checked. Keep a key with you in case it locks you out.

issues.t: Liftgate will not open from the button or remote
issues.sym: The rear hatch does not release from the button or key fob.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for liftgate release and latch problems.
issues.next: Have the liftgate latch and release checked and adjusted.

issues.t: Alarm goes off when starting or by itself
issues.sym: The perimeter alarm sounds when you start the car or goes off without a reason.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for false alarm activation.
issues.next: Ask a shop about the alarm bulletins; a sensor or module repair is usually needed.

issues.t: Brake groan, grind or squeal
issues.sym: Groaning or grinding when stopping in town, or a squeal after the brakes warm up. Rear discs may groan on the first stop after sitting overnight.
issues.why: Ford issued many bulletins for brake noise on these cars, usually fixed with revised pads.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected to make sure the noise is not worn pads.

issues.t: Starter grinding or no crank
issues.sym: A grinding noise when starting, or the starter clicks or does nothing at times.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for starter grinding on V6 automatics and for intermittent no-crank from a loose starter wire or connector.
issues.next: Have the starter wiring and mounting checked before replacing the starter.

issues.t: Headlight condensation
issues.sym: Fog or water droplets inside the headlight lenses.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for moisture inside the headlamps.
issues.next: Check the headlight seals and vents. A lens full of water may need a new headlamp.
